title: mut.channel_quayola_remains_laser_scan
mutation_directive: Quayola — Remains / Jardins d'Été — Remains: Provence (2018), Jardins d'Été (Chaumont-sur-Loire, 2022). VISUAL SIGNATURE: LiDAR point clouds of orchards and forests, rendered with the SCAN ERRORS preserved: ghostly trees made of dotted halos, missing leaves where occlusion blocked the laser, soft plastic-like blobs where foliage was too dense to resolve. Pale gray-on-near-black; reads as a tree dissolving into its own measurement noise. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: Procedurally generate a tree skeleton (L-system OR fractal), then convert it to a noisy point cloud: sample N points on each cylinder, displace each by Gaussian noise that GROWS with depth-from-camera (simulating LiDAR falloff). Some random blocks of points removed entirely (occlusion gaps). Render as PointsMaterial with size-attenuation; near-monochrome. Slow camera orbit reveals the tree as a 3D scan, not a model. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has trees (L-systems) and point clouds (Lucy) — but never a LIDAR-error tree, where the artifact IS the aesthetic. This adds the 'machine vision failing to resolve nature' signature, one of the strongest contemporary post-photography moves. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://quayola.com/remains-provence/
